{!Contact.FirstName},
Thank you for your interest in the doctor of audiology (AuD) program at Arizona State University! I look forward to assisting you as you consider your options at ASU.
About the program The AuD program is a four-year residential program that includes three years of course work and the equivalent of one year of clinical internships. It is designed to prepare audiologists for autonomous clinical practice. The audiology program is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association.
The Speech and Hearing Clinic located on the Tempe campus provides campus-based clinical training for the AuD program. The department has established affiliations with a wide variety of audiology facilities for clinical rotation opportunities for our graduate students. The greater Phoenix metropolitan area offers students clinical placements from a large selection of hospitals, clinics, private practice offices and educational facilities.
About Admission Please visit our applying to the AuD Program site at chs.asu.edu/shs/applying-aud-program and be sure to review our FAQs page at chs.asu.edu/shs/frequently-asked-questions. Here you will find more information about the application process.
We accept applications for fall only with a deadline of January 15.
You can estimate the cost of your attendance based on current tuition and fees by visiting this site: https://students.asu.edu/tuitionandfees and using our tuition calculator.
Thank you for your interest in the audiology program at Arizona State University. Please let me know if you have any questions.
Kindest regards, Anita Youmara Graduate Program Coordinator Department of Speech and Hearing Science College of Health Solutions 975 S. Myrtle Avenue | Tempe, AZ 85287 | MC 0102
